paper_title: Sound of Dark Matter: Searching for Light Scalars with Resonant-Mass Detectors
notes: Paper proposes a new resonant-mass detector concept (Cu-Si sphere, 30 cm radius) to search for light scalar dark matter moduli that couple to the electron mass (d_me) and fine-structure constant (d_e). The primary new result is a PROJECTION of sensitivity reach (blue curve in Fig. 1) after 1.6 years of integration time, spanning 1 kHz to 1 GHz (1e-6 to 1e-3 eV mass range). The paper also recasts existing AURIGA data (red curve) as a measured limit. Data points extracted from Fig. 1 blue curve (proposed Cu-Si sphere reach at SNR=1). The coupling values represent approximate strain sensitivities converted to modulus couplings via the effective strain h = -(d_me + d_e)√(4πG_N φ). Local DM density ρ_DM ≈ 0.3 GeV/cm³ is the standard galactic halo assumption used throughout. The paper constrains BOTH d_me (electron mass coupling) and d_e (electromagnetic coupling); the extracted data primarily reflects d_me sensitivity. Confidence is moderate (0.75) because: (1) the main result is a projection, not a measured limit; (2) the paper discusses multiple coupling types (d_me, d_e, and comparisons to fifth-force/EP tests); (3) data points are read from a figure rather than an explicit table. The paper is clearly motivated by scalar moduli from string theory and uses resonant-mass detector technology adapted from gravitational-wave searches. | selector: text (sole candidate)
